column1: # acmg_sf.tsv: the ACMG SF v3.3 secondary-findings genes and the reporting rule of each
# (og summary collect, rust/crates/og-summary/src/collect/acmg.rs). One row per gene, 84 rows.
# Source: Lee et al., ACMG SF v3.3
# list for reporting of secondary findings in clinical exome and genome sequencing, Genet Med
# 2026-10-27. HGNC ids from rest.genenames.org on 2026-10-27; GRCh38 positions from Ensembl.
#   gene, hgnc_id   the HGNC symbol and id
#   inheritance     AD, AR, SD (semidominant) or XL, as Table 1 gives it
#   report_if       when a P/LP variant (ClinVar, or a rare HIGH-impact record where lof allows it) is a secondary finding:
#                     biallelic       both copies of the gene hit: a homozygote, or two different
#                                     variants even when their phase is unknown (Table 1 footnote a;
#                                     reported as possibly biallelic). Two variants that read-backed
#                                     phase puts on one copy (a "|" GT and the same PS) are one copy
#                                     and are not reported; a "|" GT with no PS, or a half call such
#                                     as 1|., is phase unknown. A combined allele of step 06 counts
#                                     once with its parts, and a record with no alt copy called counts
#                                     nothing. A called deletion of the gene (AnnotSV, step 35's copy
#                                     number) counts as one of the two unless read-backed phase puts
#                                     it on the variant's copy (og-summary two_hits); so it does for
#                     hom_variant     only a variant of the variants column, homozygous
#                     hemizygous      a hemizygous or homozygous variant, or two heterozygous ones
#                                     counted as for biallelic; a single heterozygous variant is not
#                     het_female_too  any variant, heterozygous females included
#   variants        report_if hom_variant: the only variants that count, as chrom:pos:ref:alt (GRCh38)
#                   and a name; "." for every other gene
#   sv_cn           yes: an AnnotSV class 4 or 5 structural variant or copy change over the gene is a
#                   finding too (step 05); no: small variants only
#   sv_regions      other regions whose class 4 or 5 deletion counts for this gene, as chrom:start-end
#   severity        alleles that do not count as a full loss of function, separated by ";": each is
#                   hypomorph or pseudodeficiency, then chrom:pos:ref:alt, then a name. A
#                   pseudodeficiency allele is set aside; a hypomorph allele counts, but the finding says
#   sf_version      the ACMG SF list version that added the gene (Table 1)
#   table_text      Table 1's "Variants to report" text, quoted as the paper writes it: short cited
#                   quotations of a factual reporting rule (six phrases, the longest 44 characters), with
#                   the citation above. "(See text)" points to the paper's section on the dilated
#   note            what Table 1's footnotes add, in our own words, shown with the finding; "."
#   phenotype       the disease Table 1 lists the gene for (its Disease column), as a plain name
#   phenotype_keys  what a ClinVar condition of a hit (CLNDN, CLNDISDB) is matched against, separated by
#                   ";": database ids (OMIM:, MedGen:, MONDO:, Orphanet:), first Table 1's MIM disorder
#                   numbers, then phrases that must start a word of ClinVar's condition name (case, commas
#                   and dashes ignored). A hit whose every named condition matches no key is marked
#                   condition_not_acmg in summary.json and still reported; "not provided", "not
#                   specified", panel names such as "Hereditary cancer-predisposing syndrome" and a name
#                   that only names the hit's own gene ("RYR1-related disorder" on a RYR1 hit) never
#   clingen_hi      ClinGen's haploinsufficiency score of the gene as ClinGen writes it: 3 sufficient
#                   evidence, 2 some, 1 little, 0 none, 30 a gene of an autosomal recessive disease, 40
#                   dosage sensitivity unlikely; "." when ClinGen has not curated the gene. Source: ClinGen
#                   gene curation list, GRCh38, of 2026-09-07 (CC0), the archived copy
#   lof             whether a predicted loss-of-function call (a VEP HIGH-impact record) counts in the gene:
#                   yes; no (PCSK9, MYH7: their disease is no loss of function, so only a ClinVar P/LP
#                   variant counts); mark (counted, with a note that loss of function is a less certain
#                   cause: TGFBR1, TGFBR2, RBM20). A clingen_hi of 3 gives yes and 40 gives no; every other
#                   score says too little, so the gene's lof is its reviewed row of
#                   assets/acmg_lof_overrides.tsv, which also overrides a score that belongs to another
#                   disease (APOB, RET), and the build stops for a gene with neither. clingen_hi and lof are
#                   written by og dev build acmg-lof (scripts/ci/build-acmg-lof.sh); never edit them by hand
#   limit           a footnote of Table 1 that the code applies: "."; truncating_in CHROM:START-END[,...]
#                   NAME (only a stop-gained, frameshift or canonical splice variant at a position in one of
#                   those 1-based regions counts); missense_needs_case_evidence (a variant that may be
#                   missense is reported with the condition in rule_condition). TTN's cell is written by og
#                   dev build acmg-lof: ACMG SF v3.2 counts only frameshift, nonsense and splice variants of
#                   TTN exons with high PSI (Table 1 footnote f, citing Roberts et al., Sci Transl Med
#                   2015;7(270):270ra6, where high is PSI > 0.9). Its regions are the 7 runs of exons that
#                   cardiodb's titin exon table (Internet Archive copy of 2026-03-12) gives a PSI over 90%
#                   in the left ventricles of 84 DCM patients, widened by 2 bases at each end for the
#                   canonical splice sites. In LRG_391 numbering, the table's, they are exons 1-10, 13-44,
#                   exon among them; ENST00000589042 (MANE Select, NM_001267550.2) lacks
#                   LRG exon 48 (novex-3's last exon), so from LRG exon 49 on its exon number is one less
#                   (the A-band is LRG exons 253-358, Ensembl exons 252-357)
